label: copy-phase input of digit 2 (fed-back 2), from the second copy input onward
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, when the token fed back as input is the digit 2 (i.e. the model just output a 2 that was an original token). It never fires in the original or delimiter phase, even on input 2, and is essentially silent on other input tokens. When the 2 is the first copy-phase input (recall_idx 1, i.e. original token 0 was 2), it fires only weakly (~0.01-0.02 of max) or not at all; from recall_idx >= 2 it fires on every such step (precision 1.0 on dev) at roughly 0.6-1.0 of max. Remaining misses are those tiny recall_idx-1 activations plus rare faint activations on other tokens (e.g. m), together about 0.1% of activation mass.

issues: Only small issue: the misses are mainly faint (0.01-0.05 of max) activations on the first copy step (recall_idx 1) when original token 0 was 2, plus faint activations on letters such as m, s and x. Together they hold 0.13% of activation mass, which the explanation already admits to.

I checked the claims and they hold. The feature never fires in the original or delimiter phases (dev: 0 active steps in either). The phase != 2 & in_tok==2 predicate scores test F1 0.0 and precision 0.0. On test, precision is 1.000 with 0 false positives, recall 0.962, F1 0.981, mass recall 0.999 and correlation 0.989. Dropping the recall_idx >= 2 term lowers precision to 0.84 and F1 to 0.91, so that condition is justified.
